problem: Existing memory-based ImageNav methods (metric maps, stacked memory, topological maps like VGM) process all stored observations without considering which are informative, causing redundancy, distraction and deadlock, and are usually evaluated only on single-goal tasks.
motivation: Neuroscience suggests working memory selects task-relevant short-term memory and combines it with long-term memory. VGM's target-decoder attention concentrates on nodes near the goal and ignores remote ones, indicating much of the map is unhelpful. Multi-goal tasks that revisit places better test memory usefulness.
key_idea: Build a working memory for topological-map ImageNav by temporarily forgetting low-attention map nodes (STM) and adding a global aggregating node (LTM), encoded by GATv2.
insight: The LTM global node gives the largest gain in multi-goal PR (e.g. +0.056 at 3-goal, Table 4). Forgetting works best paired with the LTM, since the global node bridges sub-graphs split by removed nodes. Random forgetting hurts and training with forgetting is worse (extra ablation), so attention-based selection applied at test time matters. Optimal forgetting fraction grows with task difficulty: p=80% is best at 1-goal, but excessive forgetting hurts at 4-goal.
method: Topological map update (STM): VGM-style localization by cosine similarity with a threshold; new nodes/edges are added and node features are replaced on revisit; ResNet18 encoders.

Selective forgetting: after each Dec_target pass, nodes whose goal-attention scores rank in the bottom p% (default 20%) are disconnected and skipped at subsequent steps; they are restored if the agent revisits them and all restored when a goal is reached; plug-and-play at test time only (trained without forgetting).
Long-term memory: a zero-initialized global node linked to all map nodes, reset each episode, that aggregates STM through message passing and also bridges sub-graphs isolated by forgotten nodes.
GATv2 memory encoder: replaces VGM's 3-layer GCN with 3-layer GATv2 (feature-dependent dynamic attention) over the retained STM plus global node to produce working memory M'.
Decoding and policy: Dec_cur and Dec_target Transformer decoders (4 heads) query M' with the current and goal embeddings; an LSTM policy on [f_cur, f_target, e_cur] outputs actions.
Training: imitation learning for 20k steps, then PPO finetuning for 10M steps, following VGM; trained only on 1-goal episodes.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 encoders + GATv2 encoder + Transformer decoders + LSTM policy (trained from scratch, VGM-based)
setting.training_data: Gibson, 72 training scenes, 1-goal episodes only (IL then PPO 10M steps); multi-goal evaluated zero-shot in terms of task length
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: stop, forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 10°
setting.privileged: none (oracle stopping only for Random baseline)

numbers.eval_set_note: Gibson-based 1-goal dataset (14 unseen scenes), 1007 sampled of 1400 episodes; labelled Gibson, not HM3D, so see numbers_note
numbers.extra: forgetting p=20%, checkpoint at 9.4M PPO steps; 500-step budget, 1m success radius

numbers_note: Benchmark is Gibson ImageNav (1-goal, Mezghani et al. dataset, 14 unseen scenes) which has no exact canonical name; it was labelled HM3D-ImageNav only as the closest option, and Gibson-ImageNav is the more accurate label. Values are printed as 0.78 / 0.54 and converted to percent. Multi-goal results on the authors' own 700-episode datasets (Table 2, PR/PPL, 2-goal PR 0.50 PPL 0.17; 3-goal PR 0.42 PPL 0.09; 4-goal PR 0.31 PPL 0.05) are not listed since there is no canonical benchmark. Ablation rows on the full 1400 episodes give SR 0.610 / SPL 0.461.
results: On 1-goal Gibson MemoNav gets SR 0.78 vs VGM 0.75 (SPL 0.54 vs 0.58, lower) while using 20% fewer nodes. On multi-goal tasks PR rises from 0.45 to 0.50 (2-goal), 0.33 to 0.42 (3-goal), and 0.28 to 0.31 (4-goal) over VGM, with fewer long trajectories and less deadlock.
limitations: Forgetting is a post-hoc heuristic that needs decoder attention scores (applied with a one-step lag), uses a fixed threshold p, and does not reduce memory footprint since forgotten features are still kept for localization.
SPL/PPL is not consistently improved (1-goal SPL drops from 0.58 to 0.54), and no seed variance is reported; the multi-goal datasets are self-generated.
Main failure modes are over-exploring (49.1%) and stopping mistakenly (34.2%).
